studentTask.text: Today's focus: choosing which aspects of a topic your project will actually cover. Essential question: How do I investigate a question across sources and record what I found in my own words? By the end of this lesson you should be able to: Build an accurate model of choosing which aspects of a topic your project will actually cover from an explicit demonstration. You'll need: course notebook or an accessible digital equivalent; pencil, keyboard, or another accessible response tool; the assigned passage in print, on screen, or read aloud.

guidedSupport.text:
Work through this with a facilitator, tutor, or on your own if you're ready:
- Welcome and retrieval: Open with a brief accessible retrieval prompt connected to today's lesson. Ask the learner to recall, predict, or pose a question before any instruction.
- Word study and fluency: Two minutes of word work on the vocabulary today's lesson requires, then one short passage read for accuracy and phrasing. Reading aloud is optional.
- Model or mini-lesson: Demonstrate today's lesson with a full worked example and think aloud at each decision point.
- Guided practice: Rebuild the same example together, with the learner naming each decision.

If you get stuck:
- If prerequisite gap: Return to the smallest prerequisite today's lesson depends on, model it once with a text-only representation, then retry one fresh item.
- If decoding or fluency barrier: If the barrier is reading the words rather than today's lesson, drop to the word or phrase level, reread the line, then return. Do not reteach today's lesson while decoding is the actual obstacle.
- If repeated error pattern: Name the observable pattern neutrally, contrast it with a worked example, and schedule a short retrieval check in a later session.

independentEvidenceTask.text: The learner works one parallel item and annotates the decisions made. When finished: Explain the reasoning behind the first decision in today's lesson. What this needs to show: The learner completes the central task about choosing which aspects of a topic your project will actually cover. The learner supplies evidence, reasoning, or a documented process rather than a bare answer. The learner checks the work against the criteria and identifies a next step.

extension.text: Apply today's lesson to a longer or unfamiliar text, compare two texts on it, or teach it with an original example. Extension never means completing another learner's assessed work.
